Subject: Internal: legal position & suggested language for carve-outs

Team — read Anna's note and the external redline. High-level guidance and suggested language below. Keeping the commercial team in the loop so we can converge quickly on the call.

Summary recommendation (commercially balanced):
• Keep consequential damages excluded generally. Carve fraud and willful misconduct out of the exclusion, but subject the carve-out to a quantified threshold tied to the greater of (i) a fixed floor or (ii) a multiple of fees paid: e.g., greater of $1,000,000 or 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months.
• For gross negligence, treat as a lesser exception than fraud/willful misconduct; make it subject to a higher threshold (e.g., greater of $500,000 or 1x fees) to limit exposure.
• Define 'material breach' with a mandatory 30-day cure period and objective materiality markers (security incident resulting in data exfiltration; repeated SLA misses equal to X% of calls over Y period).

Draft excerpt (for discussion):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, neither Party shall be liable to the other for consequential, incidental, special or punitive damages, except that this exclusion shall not apply to damages resulting from (a) proven intentional fraud, (b) willful misconduct, or (c) gross negligence, each subject to the following monetary thresholds: for (a) and (b), the greater of $1,000,000 or two times the Fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim; for (c), the greater of $500,000 or one times such Fees. The foregoing shall not limit either Party's liability for claims covered by indemnities set forth in Section X (e.g., IP infringement) or for Customer Data breach obligations under Section Y."

Points for product/business input:
1) Are the proposed floors (500k / 1M) commercially acceptable for this deal band?
2) Do we have appetite for a multiple-of-fees approach vs flat numbers for predictability?
3) If Customer insists on removing 'gross negligence' from the carve-out, what's the lowest acceptable threshold?

I'll convert the draft into a tracked redline to send to Anna after your input.

—Laura

Anna — brief recap from our internal review and a proposed compromise ahead of tomorrow's 10:00 AM PT call.

We reviewed your redline and Laura prepared a responsive language that aims to balance Acme's governance needs and Redwood's exposure tolerance. Key points we propose to discuss:
• Carve-out structure: keep consequential damages excluded generally, but exclude fraud and willful misconduct from that exclusion subject to a quantified threshold. Proposed headline: greater of $750,000 or 1.5x Fees for fraud/willful misconduct; greater of $400,000 or 1x Fees for gross negligence. (These numbers reflect Priyom's input on deal band economics.)
• Material breach: include a mandatory 30-day cure period and objective triggers for termination related to security incidents or chronic SLA violations.
• We also propose limiting retroactive run-rate exposure to 12 months of Fees under the applicable Order Form to avoid open-ended liability.

Attached is our annotated redline (redline_response_v1.pdf) with Laura's suggested wording. If those headline numbers are in the right ballpark, we can narrow language on the call and lock in final phrasing.

Meeting: confirmed for 2027-04-12 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent). Dial-in in the invite.
